name: Practise asking better questions
blurb: The most underrated conversational skill. Good questions are open, specific and curious, and they are what make people find you interesting.
steps: Replace closed questions with open ones: “what was that like?” instead of “was it good?”.
Make them specific: “what surprised you about it?” beats “how was it?”.
Learn the follow-up. The second and third questions on one topic are worth more than ten first questions on ten topics.
Ask about process and feeling, not just facts: how did they decide, what did they expect.
Avoid the leading question that only invites agreement with your view.
Practise in interviews, one-to-ones and dinners, and notice which questions open people up.
tips: Rapid-fire questions feel like an interrogation. Offer something of your own between them.
“Why” can put people on the defensive. “What led to that?” asks the same thing more gently.
proof: People tell you things they say they have not told anyone else — because you asked well and then listened.
